text: dsh-login 是面向 DSH Web GUI 的多用户登录插件，接入 WebServer 网关并提供登录、首次管理员设置和退出页面。它把用户资料保存在 DSH credentials 服务中，在 GUI 设置页提供账号创建、密码重置、启用停用和删除；还提供按角色展示的设置面板、会话归属记录、默认用户工作区和主机配置管理。管理员可切换默认工作区及 remote-web-ui 兼容设置。适合需要在一个 DSH Web 部署中管理多个使用者的团队。安装后首次打开登录页即可创建管理员账号。

dsh-login adds multi-user sign-in to the DSH Web GUI with first-admin setup, login and logout. In GUI settings, administrators can create, reset, disable or remove accounts and manage workspaces and hosts. It records session ownership and exports a Remote guard for composition with typertGateway.
我想让一个 DSH Web 界面支持多个独立账号。
怎么给 DSH 网页加一个首次创建管理员的登录入口？
我希望管理员能直接在设置里新建和管理团队成员。
有没有办法给每个普通用户自动准备一个默认工作区？
我想按用户身份显示不同的 DSH 设置页面。
如何让管理员重置密码或停用一个已有账号？
我需要一个能在 DSH 网页里管理账号和主机设置的工具。
I want separate accounts for people using one DSH web interface.
Can each new user get a ready-to-use workspace automatically?
I need an admin page to add users and reset their passwords.
dsh-login 的功能「登录与首次设置」：首次打开 /login 时显示管理员创建表单，已有账号时显示用户名和密码登录页；提交后创建会话，用户也可退出。
dsh-login 的功能「用户管理」：管理员可在 GUI 设置面板查看账号、创建普通用户或管理员、重置密码、启用停用及删除账号。
dsh-login 的功能「角色设置面板」：客户端先读取当前用户身份，再为管理员注入用户管理区，为普通用户注入账户信息与退出入口。
dsh-login 的功能「Remote 用户隔离组合」：导出的网关包装器根据用户角色、允许的方法和会话归属检查 invoke 与 stream 请求。
dsh-login 的功能「默认用户工作区」：普通用户首次访问 API 时可自动创建个人工作区并附加一个会话；管理员能在设置页切换此功能。
dsh-login 的功能「主机设置」：管理员可在设置面板查看、添加和移除受信任主机，并切换默认工作区与 remote-web-ui 兼容选项。
dsh-login 的功能「Web 网关」：通过 DSH WebServer 的 fallback 路由呈现认证后的前端页面，并根据账号角色筛选客户端启动清单。
dsh-login 将 Remote 会话隔离作为可组合的网关工具导出；部署需要将它接入原生 typertGateway，入口不会自动替换该服务。

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · dsh-login：English | [简体中文](./README.zh.md)

Adds a **login page, user accounts, and per-user conversation isolation** to the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web GUI: every visit requires sign-in, ordinary users cannot see each other's conversations, and an admin manages all accounts from inside the GUI.

| Login page | User management (设置 → 用户管理) |
|:---:|:---:|
|  |  |

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · The problem it solves：The DSH Web GUI ships with **no login** — it assumes a single user on localhost. The moment you bind it to `0.0.0.0` (phone access, LAN sharing, a small team), **anyone on that network can open your GUI**: read every conversation, burn your configured model API keys, even change host settings.

`dsh-login` turns that exposure into a multi-user deployment:

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · The problem it solves：- 🔐 **Login wall** — pages, static assets, SPA routes, the API, and WebSockets all require a valid session; unauthenticated visitors are redirected to `/login`
- 👥 **Multiple accounts** — the first visit creates the administrator account; further users are added by an admin right inside the GUI, no CLI needed
- 🙈 **Conversation isolation** — ordinary users see and act on **their own** conversations only (including their subagents/forks); the bridge wall denies non-whitelisted methods and narrows `session.list`/`session.search`/`workspace.list` responses to owned sessions, and the composed REMOTE-layer guard scopes dispatches by ownership; other users' sessions, messages, and workspaces are invisible; credentials, host settings, and other admin domains are forbidden wholesale
- 🛠 **User management** — 设置 → 用户管理: last-login time, online session count, reset password, disable, remove; disabling/removing/password-changes **immediately revoke** that user's live sessions
- 👑 **Admin exception** — the admin is not isolated: all sessions visible, full configuration access
- 🚪 **Logout** — every user gets a logout entry in their settings

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · What installation does：`dsh plugin add` reads this package's declared `cordis.patch.yml` (a bundle patch) and automatically:
@islibaodong/dsh-login README · Manual installation (alternative)：If you prefer managing the patch file yourself, add these rows to your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · Manual installation (alternative)：```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-login
      name: '@islibaodong/dsh-login'
      config:
        password: DSH_LOGIN_PASSWORD   # credential ref name; namespaces the user store (<name>_USERS)
        distIndex: ''                  # empty resolves the frontend dist automatically
        dataDir: ''                    # empty resolves to <DSH_HOME>/.dsh-login (ownership index)
        sessionTtl: 604800             # 7 days (default)
        autoTrustHosts: true          # learn the Host of any successful login into the /api whitelist
        enabled: true                 # set false to disable without uninstalling
        defaultWorkspace: true        # auto-provision a per-user default workspace on first /api access (on by default; toggleable live in 设置-用户管理)
        workspaceRoot: ''             # default-workspace sandbox root; empty => <DSH_HOME>/workspaces
        apiBridgeAuth: true           # require the dsh_session cookie on the shared /api bridge (DSH >= 0.1.6-alpha.2, on by default)

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · webRuntime service, so the rest of the composition is unaffected.：- id: web-runtime
  disabled: true
```
> The shipped `connection` row (dsh-client-connection) stays **enabled** in option A —
> it owns `/api` and the browser-session auth. Do not disable it. dsh-login ships a
> ready-made deployment glue for per-user isolation (see [`docs/compose-guard.md`](docs/compose-guard.md)):
> fork your `typertGateway` row and wrap the native gateway with `composeDshLoginGuard`
> at boot — dsh-login publishes its ownership sidecar as the `dshLoginOwnership` service
> for exactly that composition.

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · First-time setup flow：1. **First visit** (no users yet) -> `/login` shows a "Create administrator account" page (username + password)
2. User picks credentials -> `POST /api/auth/setup` creates the forced-admin account (scrypt-hashed, stored under the `${password}_USERS` credential ref, default `DSH_LOGIN_PASSWORD_USERS`) and logs it in
3. **Subsequent visits** -> `/login` shows the normal username/password login form
4. **User management** -> admins open 设置 → 用户管理 in the GUI to list (last login/online status), create, disable/enable, remove users and reset passwords (`/api/auth/admin/*` JSON routes; removing the last admin is refused)
5. **Security** -> `/api/auth/setup` returns 403 once any user exists, preventing hijacking

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · First-time setup flow：> **Migration note:** the legacy single-password credential (default ref `DSH_LOGIN_PASSWORD`) no longer logs anyone in. It stays configured but is unused for authentication — the `password` config key now only namespaces the user store credential ref (`${password}_USERS`). Upgrading an existing single-password deployment therefore requires the first visit to bootstrap a fresh administrator account.

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · How it works：```
Request -> WebServer
  ├─ /login (exact)            -> dsh-login: setup page (if no users) OR login page
  ├─ /api/auth/setup (exact)  -> dsh-login: POST create admin on first use (403 if users exist)
  ├─ /api/auth/login (exact)  -> dsh-login: POST verify {username,password}, set cookie

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · Multi-user permission model：- **Ordinary users are conversation-only.** In option A the native `connection`/`api-gateway` owns `/api` and is agent-keyed. Two layers now enforce the boundary:
  1. **Method allow-list on the bridge wall (`apiBridgeAuth`, always on with the wall):** a non-admin POST whose wire endpoint (`/api/<endpoint>`, dotted like `session.create`) is not on the `USER_ALLOWED` allow-list is denied — with `quietDenials` (default) as a wire-correct forbidden envelope, otherwise a plain 403. `GET`/SSE/WS pass through to the upstream fence (the wire is POST-only).
  2. **REMOTE-layer isolation guard (`wrapRemoteGateway`, exported from this package), composed over `typertGateway` via the deployment glue** ([`docs/compose-guard.md`](docs/compose-guard.md)): restricts ordinary users to their **own** sessions plus lineage children (subagents/forks — ownership follows `parentSessionId`), scoped by the ownership sidecar the wall keeps warm.
  - **Response narrowing on the bridge wall:** `session.list` / `session.search` / `workspace.list` responses of an ordinary user are filtered down to their owned sessions (workspaces keep only owned `sessi

|------|----------|
| User accounts (scrypt hashes) | DSH credentials system, ref `${password}_USERS` (default `DSH_LOGIN_PASSWORD_USERS`) |
| Session→user ownership sidecar | `<DSH_HOME>/.dsh-login/ownership.json` (configurable via `dataDir`; `DSH_HOME` env or `~/.dsh`) |
| Auto-learned / admin Host whitelist | `<DSH_HOME>/.dsh-login/trusted-hosts.json` (configurable via `dataDir`) |

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · `/api` integration (option A, DSH ≥ 0.1.5-alpha.1)：For DSH ≥ 0.1.5-alpha.1 dsh-login **no longer takes over the `/api` carrier**: `cordis.patch.yml`
leaves the shipped `connection` row enabled, so `dsh-client-connection` + `api-remotes` /
`api-gateway` own the `/api` transport and the live Remote streams. dsh-login composes its
per-user layer on top of that native stack (see [`docs/adapt-dsh-0.1.5.md`](docs/adapt-dsh-0.1.5.md)
and the verification checklist [`docs/verify-option-A.md`](docs/verify-option-A.md)):
fallback login wall + static serving through the native `serveStatic`, plus
`connection.authorizeIndex` on index responses so the browser receives its upstream `/api`
cookie. The old `src/connection.ts` carrier takeover and its `dist/client.js` re-stamp were
removed with the `dsh-host-apiproxy`-based per-user `ApiProxy`. The per-user conversation /
workspace isolation is re-homed as a REMOTE-layer guard — `wrapRemoteGateway` +
`createRemoteIsolation`, exported from this package's host bundle and unit/integration-tested —
which a deployment composes over the native `typertGateway` at boot using the shipped glue
(dsh-login publishes its ownershi

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · `/api` integration (option A, DSH ≥ 0.1.5-alpha.1)：**Host trust is evaluated live per request.** The `/api` fence uses a deduped effective set —
LAN literals from the web runtime + `trustedHosts` + the persisted whitelist (`src/hosts.ts`).
A successful login/setup auto-learns the request Host (gated by `autoTrustHosts`, default
true), so a public host reached through frp/隧道/tunnels is trusted after one login; learned
hosts bind immediately and removals apply without a restart.

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · Protected by the gateway：| Asset | Protection |
|-------|-----------|
| Page navigation (`/`) | 302 redirect to `/login` if unauthenticated |
| Static assets (`/assets/*.js`, `.css`, etc.) | Same gateway check |
| SPA routes (`/conversations`, `/settings`, etc.) | Same gateway check |

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · Protected by the gateway：**The process launch token never reaches remote clients (issue #10).** The
core mints one random launch token per process; `dsh web` prints the
`/?token=…` URL in the **local console only**, and that token is what mints
the browser cookie and what `GET /connect` exchanges for an owner-principal
API credential. Earlier releases bootstrapped a fresh device by bouncing the
browser to `/?token=<launchToken>`, which exposed the token to the remote
client (Location header → browser history, proxy access logs) — dsh-login
0.3.9 instead runs the same exchange server-side and serves the index
directly with the minted cookie, so the token never appears on the wire. A
remote user can therefore never reach owner credentials through dsh-login;
the token remains a local-console-only secret, exactly as upstream delivers
it.

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · Protected by the bridge wall：| Asset | Protection |
|-------|-----------|
| API requests (`/api/*`) | `isTrustedApiRequest` host trust **and** a valid `dsh_session` cookie (401 without one); non-allowed POST methods denied for ordinary users (wire-correct forbidden envelope with `quietDenials`, else 403); `session.list`/`session.search`/`workspace.list` responses narrowed to owned sessions |
| WebSocket (`/api/events.mux`, `/api/events.host`) | Host-trust + browser-auth checks on upgrade (upstream fence — no per-request hook exists there); per-user frame filtering is provided by the composed REMOTE-layer guard, not the upgrade fence |
@islibaodong/dsh-login README · Recommendations for public exposure：**Troubleshooting: a non-admin user "cannot add a workspace" over a public tunnel?**

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · Recommendations for public exposure：Diagnosis quick reference: this is almost never the host whitelist (autoTrustHosts already learns the public host and login succeeds). On **≤ 0.3.5** the blocker was the method gate: the frontend's add-workspace flow calls the directory picker, and 0.3.5's `USER_ALLOWED` carried the pre-0.2 spellings (`host.pickDirectory`, …), so non-admins were denied with `not permitted for this user` / `HTTP 403`. **0.3.6 fixes exactly this** (issue #4): the real picker is `directoryPicker.pick`/`list`/`createDirectory` and it is admitted to ordinary users.

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · Architecture note: fallback vs prefix /：The gateway uses `registerFallback()` (not `register({ kind: 'prefix', path: '/' })`) because the DSH WebServer's prefix matching checks `pathname.startsWith(prefix + '/')`. For prefix `/`, this becomes `//`, which no normal path starts with -- a `prefix /` route only matches the exact path `/`. The fallback handler catches everything no named route claims, which is the correct catch-all behavior for the authentication gateway.

@islibaodong/dsh-login README · Architecture note: fallback vs prefix /：The WebServer has a single fallback seat. dsh-web-app's `web-runtime` row mounts frontend-static over it unconditionally, so the `web-runtime` row must be disabled when using `dsh-login`; dsh-login re-provides the `webRuntime` service that row owned (LAN trust, `DSH_WEB_URL`), leaving the rest of the composition intact.

The `connection` / `api-filter` / `multiuser-e2e` specs were **removed** in the option-A adaptation (they tested the deleted `dsh-host-apiproxy` `/api` takeover); the REMOTE-layer isolation guard is covered by `tests/remote-guard.spec.ts` (ownership scoping, admin passthrough, array/nested id-arg ownership) and the bridge wall (401 + method gate + quiet denials + record/filter tee + provisioning trigger) by `tests/api-bridge-auth.spec.ts`. `tests/runner.mjs` and `tests/integration-runner.mjs` are sandbox-compatible harnesses for the original single-password core only; they were not extended for the multi-user feature. The live two-browser isolation sign-off (§B of `docs/verify-option-A.md`) still requires a booted deployment.
